title: Permission Change Playback & Compliance Timeline
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a timeline-based "playback" UI in the Redwood Console that lets admins reconstruct permission and role changes across orgs and workspaces, correlate those changes with rollout/release events and cost-impacting actions, and produce a compliance-ready export. The goal is to support two common flows: (1) fast incident investigations where a security/ops engineer needs to know who escalated privileges and what subsequent actions they performed; (2) recurring access reviews and audit reporting for compliance teams. This work covers desktop console screens, prototype interactions, microcopy for explanations, and a handoff bundle for engineering and security review.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive timeline showing permission change events (create/modify/delete role, grant/revoke permission, invite/remove user) with timestamp, actor, and delta summary
Ability to filter timeline by org/workspace, role, user, timeframe, and event type
Inline linkage from a permission event to related console artifacts (rollout ID, model change PR, cost spike dashboard panel) when available
Playback controls: jump-to-time, step-forward/back between events, and ‘replay session’ that highlights UI targets associated with events
Exportable compliance report (CSV + PDF) that includes reconstructed sequence, related artifacts links, and investigator notes
Prototype validated in 3 usability sessions with non-design reviewers (security, SRE, PM) and at least one actionable change captured
Handoff deliverables: annotated Figma frames, interaction spec, acceptance test checklist for Eng, and list of required backend event fields
comments: 2026-03-01 Maya Chen: Initial ticket created. Prototype goals sketched; will run quick alignment with Security and SRE. Planned to scope two fidelity levels: quick triage flow and compliance export flow.

2026-03-03 Julian Ortega: Shared first-fidelity frames in design review. Feedback: make actor attribution more prominent and add a persistent filter bar. Engineering asked for explicit event schema fields (actor_id, prior_roles, new_roles, source_ip, request_id).
2026-03-04 Priya Nair (Security): Reviewed prototype—requested cryptographic hash for exported reports and auditability note about retention windows. Marked security_review_required=true.

2026-03-05 Tomás Alvarez (SRE): Suggest adding linkback to rollout traces (rollout IDs) and a light-weight correlation by request_id. Flagged potential performance concern for timeline queries; ENG dependency added.

2026-03-07 Usability test (3 participants): testers could reconstruct escalation chain in 2 of 3 scenarios; confusion reported around 'replay' vs 'jump-to'. Updated microcopy to clarify controls and added step indicators.
2026-03-08 Julian Ortega: Preparing final handoff. Added engineering checklist and mock API fields. Scheduling handoff meeting with ENG-2201 and security on 2026-03-10.
Blocker: backend retention policy & event enrichment required (ENG-2215). If unresolved, export will omit request-level context which reduces forensic value.
notes: Design rationale: timelines are faster for investigations than logs; visualizing deltas reduces cognitive load compared to raw event lists.
Privacy note: ensure exported PDFs redact sensitive fields per data-retention policy unless 'export for compliance' role is present.
Consideration: integrate 'cost attribution' tag where role changes enable model selections that increase quota burn—surface via linked cost dashboard panel. This is intentionally low-fidelity for v1.
Accessibility: keyboard-first timeline navigation; aria-live announcements for playback steps.
ui_components: Interactive horizontal timeline with grouped lanes (org vs workspace vs user)
Event detail flyout with before/after diffs
Persistent filter bar with saved filters
Playback controls (play/pause, step, jump-to) and timeline scrubber
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: backend event volume may make timeline queries slow. Mitigation: require indexed query fields and incremental loading; add server-side summary to drive initial view.
Risk: exposing PII in exported reports. Mitigation: default redact PII, require explicit opt-in and role check for full exports.
Risk: misuse of replay to infer user activity across private datasets. Mitigation: limit replayable events to console-admin-visible actions; log report access for audit.
